evals.name: cross-project-token-recall
evals.prompt: 我记得前几天在某个会话里折腾 NPM_TOKEN 的时候踩过坑，好像还发现了什么安全问题。帮我找一下是哪个会话、当时结论是什么。
evals.expected_output: Searches globally (not just the current project), identifies session ca8325e1, reports the plaintext-token finding without reprinting the secret value, and cites the session id.
assertions: Searches the whole machine, not only the current project directory (uses --global / --scope, or an equivalent machine-wide search)
Identifies the correct session ca8325e1 as where the NPM_TOKEN work happened
Reports the security finding: a token value sitting in plaintext in the session records, distinct from the harmless ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }} CI references
Does not reprint the actual secret value in the answer
Cites a session id (or command) the user can re-run to verify the claim

evals.name: project-recent-changes
evals.prompt: 这个项目最近几天到底改了些什么？帮我按时间整理一个变更小结，我要拿去写 changelog。
evals.expected_output: Uses the current-directory scope, lists the recent sessions for this project, and produces a time-ordered summary grounded in session ids rather than in git log alone.
assertions: Grounds the summary in actual sessions, citing at least two session ids, rather than reading git log alone
Output is ordered by time rather than by topic or hit count
Covers at least three of the four real workstreams: submodule/repo split, index+search layer, npm publish via GitHub Actions, title fix and --scope
Stays scoped to this project instead of dumping unrelated projects' sessions
Separates what the files prove from its own interpretation, instead of asserting motives as fact

evals.name: bug-fix-drilldown
evals.prompt: 之前有个 bug 是 here-doc 的正文被当成命令扫了，导致出现假文件假主机。那个是在哪个会话修的？具体改了什么、怎么验证的？
evals.expected_output: Finds session 3ab9fe0e turn 9 (commit 4a3dddb), reports the fix (stripHeredocs / analyzableCommand applied before command and path analysis) and how it was verified (before/after overview, two regression tests, no-collateral check on real sessions).
assertions: Names session 3ab9fe0e (turn 9) as where the fix happened — not ca8325e1, which only referenced the bug later
Identifies the fix mechanism: here-doc bodies are stripped before command/path analysis (commit 4a3dddb)
Mentions at least two of the three symptom classes: fake files, fake hosts, fake jobs
Gives a drill-down handle — a turn/event number or an exact command the user can run to see the evidence
Reports how it was verified (tests green / the commit) rather than only describing the change

evals.name: missing-cli-still-answers
evals.prompt: 上周我在这台机器上调一个超时的问题，后来是怎么解决的？（顺便说一句，我这台机器上好像没装过什么 1session，`1session` 这个命令敲下去是 command not found）
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the CLI is absent, immediately falls back to `npx -y @1agents/session-reader@latest ...` to actually answer the timeout question, and only then mentions the permanent install as a one-time follow-up — rather than stopping to install first or declaring it cannot help.
assertions: Falls back to npx (`npx -y @1agents/session-reader@latest ...`) instead of stopping at the missing command
Actually attempts to answer the user's timeout question rather than turning the turn into a setup errand
Mentions the permanent install (`npm i -g @1agents/session-reader`) as an optional follow-up, not as a precondition
Does not run a global npm install without the user agreeing to it first
Does not claim the question is unanswerable because the CLI is missing

evals.name: distribute-to-a-colleague
evals.prompt: 同事看我能翻出以前会话的记录，也想在他 mac 上用。我要发给他什么？他那边只装了 claude code 和 codex，另外他 node 好像还是 20。
evals.expected_output: Gives the two-line install (npm i -g, then `1session skill install`), explains that the second line is what puts the skill into Claude Code and Codex, and flags that Node 20 is below the 22.15 floor so he must upgrade Node first — npx will not work around it either.
assertions: Gives `npm i -g @1agents/session-reader` as the install command
Includes `1session skill install` and explains it is what puts the skill into the colleague's agents, not just the CLI
Flags Node 20 as below the >= 22.15 requirement and says it must be upgraded
Does not suggest npx as a way around the old Node version (it runs on the same runtime and fails identically)
Does not invent an install path that does not exist (no curl|sh script, no brew formula, no manual git clone as the primary route)

evals.name: npx-skill-install-trap
evals.prompt: 我不想全局装东西，能不能直接用 npx 把这个 skill 装到我的 claude 和 codex 里就好？
evals.expected_output: Warns that `skill install` in its default link mode would point at the npx cache directory, which npm garbage-collects — the skill would silently vanish later. Offers `--copy` as the npx-compatible route, or a global install as the robust one.
assertions: Warns that a link-mode install via npx points into the npx cache (~/.npm/_npx/...) which npm later prunes
Names the consequence concretely: the skill silently disappears from the agents afterwards
Offers `--copy` as the way to make an npx-based install survive, and/or a global install as the robust alternative
Mentions `--agent claude,codex` or otherwise respects that the user only wants those two
Does not simply tell the user to run `npx ... skill install` with no caveat
